assumption_inventory: The underlying measure is finite and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. The Euclidean-valued standard Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
Each coordinate integrand is progressive and square-integrable for the product of the horizon time measure and the underlying measure. The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality.
The horizon T is positive. At each deterministic time t≤T, the drift Aₜ is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Almost every drift path is continuous and has bounded variation on [0,T].
The cutoff τ is any fixed grid point of a specified coarse dyadic grid on [0,T].
units.statement: Let X be the sum of a drift with almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on [0,T] and a finite row of completed scalar Itô integrals. The integrals are driven by the coordinates of a standard vector Brownian motion relative to the given filtration and measure. For a fixed coarse dyadic time τ, the prefix sums of squared fine-grid increments of X converge in measure to the integrated squared row norm up to τ.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Stop the drift by a monotone time change
substantive_formula_moves.text: The map that clips time at τ is continuous, nondecreasing and maps the horizon into itself. Its composition with the drift preserves the path conditions and has almost-everywhere measurable evaluations at each time.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Apply stopped quadratic variation
substantive_formula_moves.text: The fixed time is a bounded stopping time. With the clipped drift, the existing stopped-row theorem gives convergence of the squared increments of the full stopped process to the restricted energy.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Replace stopped increments by the prefix
substantive_formula_moves.text: Every sufficiently fine grid refines the chosen coarse grid. The deterministic cutoff identity with both paths equal to X gives exact equality of the two sums at those levels.

units.scope_boundary: The theorem concerns one fixed dyadic cutoff and convergence in measure for the unweighted scalar sum. Mixed and continuously weighted limits are separate results.
units.proof_topology: clip-time variation; deterministic stopping; exact fine/coarse dyadic alignment
dependency_edges: monotone continuous composition preserves bounded variation
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Need common full-measure path events and exact alignment for every n>=m; hypotheses provide this. No natural defect found.

assumption_inventory: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The grid lies in [0,T] and is nondecreasing. The coordinate index type J is finite and may be empty.
For each j, both integrands are real, progressive and square integrable. They share the same Brownian motion Bⱼ relative to the given filtration. The drivers at different indices may be dependent.
units.statement: For each of finitely many coordinates, integrate two progressive square-integrable integrands against the same coordinate Brownian motion. Sum the resulting coordinate integrals to form each row. The difference of their squared-increment sums is integrable, and its expected absolute value is bounded uniformly over finite deterministic grids.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Factor the difference of squares
substantive_formula_moves.text: At the two deterministic endpoints in each cell, linearity identifies the increments of the sum and difference of the integrands. Multiply these two increments and add over cells.
substantive_formula_moves.formula: Q(\eta)-Q(\xi)=\sum_i U_iV_i\quad\mu\text{-a.e.},\qquad U_i=\Delta_i R_{\eta+\xi},\quad V_i=\Delta_i R_{\eta-\xi}.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz twice
substantive_formula_moves.text: Each row increment is in L² by the scalar cell isometries and finite summation. The products are therefore integrable, as is the signed difference. Bound the absolute value of the finite sum by the sum of the absolute products. Apply integral Cauchy–Schwarz in each cell, then finite Cauchy–Schwarz to the resulting list of square roots.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Control the row energies
substantive_formula_moves.text: Cauchy–Schwarz across the coordinates bounds the square of each row increment by the coordinate count times the sum of the coordinate squares. Apply the exact scalar grid isometry to each coordinate and enlarge the grid span to [0,T]. Each square root contributes a factor √|J|.

units.scope_boundary: The inequality compares the two actual row processes on any common deterministic grid. The squared-increment limit needs a separate proof for an approximating family.
units.proof_topology: factor Q(eta)-Q(xi); two Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities; scalar grid isometry; coordinate-count energy bound
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: The |J| factor allows dependent drivers; no cross-coordinate orthogonality should be assumed. Empty J yields zero. No natural defect found.

assumption_inventory: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The integrand is a dyadic elementary adapted process with its bounded, left-endpoint measurable cell coefficients.

The scalar driver is Brownian under μ relative to the given filtration. It is the driver for both the completed integral and the increment on the right. The chosen cell belongs to the elementary process's own grid.
units.statement: On any cell of an adapted dyadic elementary integrand's own grid, its completed Itô integral increment agrees almost surely with the cell coefficient times the corresponding Brownian increment.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Identify the endpoint values
substantive_formula_moves.text: At a positive deterministic grid point, use the terminal restriction identity for the elementary integrand. At time zero, both constructions have zero value.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Keep only the selected cell
substantive_formula_moves.text: Expand the difference of the elementary sums. Earlier cells are complete at both endpoints. Later cells contribute zero at both endpoints. The selected cell gives the displayed coefficient times the driver increment.

units.scope_boundary: The equality is almost sure for each chosen cell of the elementary process's own deterministic grid.
units.proof_topology: identify completed/elementary endpoint values; cancel previous/later cells
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: The endpoint equality must use the same scalar Brownian driver and chosen elementary grid. No natural defect found.

assumption_inventory: $I$ is a finite coordinate set. $w$ is in the Euclidean unit sphere. The field $u$ is ambient-vector-valued and the temperature function is real-valued.
units.statement: For an ambient field $u$ and a real temperature function $\lambda$, the drift at a unit vector is the negative field plus the radial correction. The definition returns its $i$th coordinate.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Evaluate the vector field and radial term
substantive_formula_moves.text: Multiply the state by the temperature and ambient dimension minus one, then subtract this vector along with the field.

units.scope_boundary: The formula is an ambient drift coefficient. The hypotheses of an actual diffusion are supplied when the coefficient is used in a stochastic equation.
units.proof_topology: evaluate ambient drift coordinate
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: No diffusion existence or tangency follows from this definition. Unit sphere forces nonempty dimension whenever a state is supplied.

assumption_inventory: The domain is a complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.
The vector Brownian motion is adapted to the stated filtration, with future vector increments independent of its past.
units.statement: A norm-one continuous linear functional of a standard Hilbert-space Brownian motion gives a real Brownian motion relative to the original filtration.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Read the projected law
substantive_formula_moves.text: The variance of a projected increment is elapsed time times the squared operator norm.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Keep the original filtration
substantive_formula_moves.text: Projection preserves continuity and adaptedness. The projected future increment generates a sub-sigma-algebra of the original vector increment.

units.scope_boundary: Unit norm gives standard scalar normalization.
units.proof_topology: project Gaussian increment laws; preserve continuity/adaptation; shrink increment sigma-algebra
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: The written proof compresses the bridge from projected increment laws and independence to all scalar finite-dimensional distributions; this is a required prerequisite, not an added assumption.

assumption_inventory: All coordinates are from one Euclidean Brownian driver with the stated filtration.
Every row coefficient is strongly measurable at its cell’s left endpoint, in L⁴, and subject to one uniform fourth-moment bound.
The coordinate type is finite. The horizon may be zero.
units.statement: The compensated sum of the squares of actual diffusion-row increments is in L² on each dyadic grid and converges to zero in mean square.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Control the product weights
substantive_formula_moves.text: The average of two fourth powers bounds the square of the product. This gives the L² domain and the required uniform second moments.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Apply the diagonal and mixed results
substantive_formula_moves.text: The diagonal subtracts the elapsed time; distinct coordinates use the actual mixed increment product.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Expand the actual row square
substantive_formula_moves.text: Expanding the square and the compensator gives the finite sum over all ordered coordinate pairs.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Transfer the finite-sum limit
substantive_formula_moves.text: Each pair sum is square integrable and its squared expectation tends to zero. The square of the whole sum is bounded by the number of pairs times the sum of squares.

units.scope_boundary: The coefficients are the specified grid rows. A continuous approximation has separate integrability and convergence obligations.
units.proof_topology: control products by fourth moments; diagonal/mixed QV; expand ordered coordinate pairs; finite-sum L2 bound
dependency_edges: Holder product L4 x L4 into L2
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Uniform fourth-moment bounds must be uniform over levels, cells and coordinate indices as stated. No natural defect found.

assumption_inventory: The horizon T is positive. The real weight w is continuous on [0,T].
The real density b is integrable for the time measure on [0,T].
units.statement: Multiply each increment of the drift primitive by the continuous weight at the left endpoint. The dyadic sums converge to the time integral of the weight times the original density.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Read each prefix increment
substantive_formula_moves.text: The difference of two strict prefixes is the integral over the half-open interval from the left endpoint. Each deterministic endpoint has zero time measure, so the integral agrees with the right-closed cell integral.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Take the left samples to the weight
substantive_formula_moves.text: Every positive time through T lies in one cell. Its left endpoint approaches the time, so its sampled weight converges. Compact continuity gives a common bound, and |b| is integrable.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Identify the finite sums
substantive_formula_moves.text: Integrating the piecewise left weight times b gives exactly the sum of the weighted prefix increments. Apply the dominated limit to this identity.

units.scope_boundary: The convergence is a deterministic real limit along the full dyadic grid.
units.proof_topology: convert strict-prefix differences to right-closed cell integrals; approximate continuous weight by left samples; dominated convergence
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Endpoint zero has null time measure and must be excluded or treated in the pointwise step. Source states 0<t<=T. No defect found.

assumption_inventory: The horizon T is nonnegative. Both paths are continuous on [0,T].
The path A has finite total variation on [0,T]. The path X may have infinite total variation.
units.statement: Add a continuous bounded-variation path A to a continuous real path X. The signed change in the sum of squared increments tends to zero on the full dyadic grid over the horizon.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Bound the total increments of A
substantive_formula_moves.text: The grid is nondecreasing, so the sum of the absolute increments of A is at most its total variation. At T=0 every grid increment is zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Factor the square difference
substantive_formula_moves.text: Expand both squares. Each term is the increment of A times a combination of the two path increments.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Use continuity on the compact interval
substantive_formula_moves.text: As the mesh shrinks, both largest increments vanish by uniform continuity. Multiply their combined bound by the finite total variation.

units.scope_boundary: The statement gives the signed difference limit. Setting X=0 gives zero quadratic variation for a continuous finite-variation path.
units.proof_topology: bound variation sum; factor difference of squares; uniform continuity makes maximal increments vanish
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: T=0 is handled separately; no bounded variation for X or stochastic hypotheses needed. No defect found.

assumption_inventory: A progressive, real, product-space L² integrand on a positive deterministic horizon T with finite sample measure μ.
One scalar Brownian motion under μ relative to the given filtration. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
The deterministic endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ T.
The event A is measurable in the filtration at time s. The evaluation time u is any fixed time in [0,T].
units.statement: Restrict a progressive integrand to the cell (s,t] and an event known at s. The restricted process is progressive and square integrable. Its completed Itô integral at each fixed time is the original cell increment, truncated at that time, multiplied by the event indicator.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Switch between two stopping times
substantive_formula_moves.text: Take the stop to be t on A and s on its complement. The event and its complement are already known at s, so Mathlib's piecewise constant theorem applies.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Subtract the two closed stopped inputs
substantive_formula_moves.text: Subtract the input stopped at s from the input stopped at the switch. This yields the exact pointwise event and cell restriction.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Use linearity and stopping compatibility
substantive_formula_moves.text: The completed integral of the difference equals the difference of the two completed stopped integrals. Evaluate each one at the capped time.

units.scope_boundary: The integral identity is for each deterministic evaluation time. The restriction of the integrand is pointwise.
units.proof_topology: construct switching stop; subtract closed stopped inputs; use linearity and stopping compatibility
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: The stochastic identity is for each fixed evaluation time, not automatically one common full-measure event for all times. Source keeps this scope.

assumption_inventory: A progressive, real, product-space L² integrand on a positive deterministic horizon T with finite sample measure μ.
One scalar Brownian motion under μ relative to the given filtration. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
The deterministic endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ T.
The multiplier w is strongly measurable at s and satisfies |w(ω)|≤C pointwise for a real bound C.
units.statement: Multiply the input on one Itô cell by a bounded real random variable known at the left endpoint. The literal weighted input is progressive and square integrable. Its terminal integral agrees almost surely with the weight times the original completed increment.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Construct the literal weighted input
substantive_formula_moves.text: The unweighted cell process vanishes up to s. At later times the left-endpoint multiplier is available in the filtration. Multiplication by the bounded variable preserves the product L² condition.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Prove the identity for simple weights
substantive_formula_moves.text: Each fiber of a finite-range simple weight is a past event. Apply the event multiplier to each fiber, scale by its value and add the resulting integrals.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Pass to the original bounded multiplier
substantive_formula_moves.text: Approximate w pointwise by simple weights taking values in the same compact interval. The squared product errors are dominated by the square of the unweighted cell process times a finite constant, giving product-space L² convergence.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Identify the two limits
substantive_formula_moves.text: The terminal Itô isometry carries the L² convergence to convergence in measure on the sample space. The weighted original increments also converge pointwise. Uniqueness of the limit in measure gives the identity.

units.scope_boundary: The output is the terminal integral of an input supported on (s,t]. The time cell may be empty.
units.proof_topology: construct literal weighted process; simple-weight event decomposition; dominated L2 approximation; uniqueness in measure
dependency_edges: simple measurable approximants on compact interval
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Need past measurability for every approximation and integrability of squared product errors. Source indicates both routes. No natural defect found.

assumption_inventory: One actual finite-dimensional Euclidean Brownian motion under a finite sample measure μ, relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions.
A positive deterministic horizon T, one common finite-valued stopping time with τ(ω)≤T at every sample point, and progressive product-space L² input in each coordinate.
The drift A is almost surely continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T]. Its deterministic-time values are almost everywhere strongly measurable. No moment of the total variation is required.
units.statement: Add a continuous finite-variation drift to a finite row of original completed Itô integrals evaluated at a common bounded stop. The squared dyadic increments of the sum converge in measure to the original integrated square energy up to the stop.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Check the stopped row as a process
substantive_formula_moves.text: The stopped coordinate integrals are adapted and are continuous along the paths. Finite sums give the same properties for the row and give measurability of its square-increment sums.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Use the stopped Itô bracket limit
substantive_formula_moves.text: The stopped row's squared increments converge in L¹ to the literal stopped energy. Therefore they converge to that energy in measure.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Pass through the drift perturbation
substantive_formula_moves.text: The deterministic perturbation theorem holds on the full-measure event of continuous finite variation. Every subsequence of the stopped row squares has a further almost surely convergent subsequence. Add the vanishing pathwise drift difference and use the subsequence criterion.

units.scope_boundary: The supplied drift is evaluated at time t and the Itô row at t∧τ. A drift that has already been stopped can be supplied. The conclusion is convergence in measure.
units.proof_topology: regularity of stopped row; L1 bracket limit implies in-measure limit; pathwise drift perturbation and subsequences
dependency_edges: bounded stopped Ito row L1 QV
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: A is not stopped in this statement; only the row is. Source boundary correctly distinguishes this. No variation moment is needed.

assumption_inventory: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. The space is real Euclidean space on I.
The coordinate j belongs to I and x is any ambient vector.
units.statement: For any j in I and any ambient vector x, take the j-th coordinate vector and subtract x_j times x.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Apply the rank-one formula to one coordinate
substantive_formula_moves.text: The inner product of x with the coordinate vector e_j is x_j. This is the action of the matrix I−xxᵀ on e_j.

units.scope_boundary: On the unit sphere this column is tangent.
units.proof_topology: rank-one column formula
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: A definition on all ambient points; tangent interpretation only at norm-one states.

assumption_inventory: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. The space is real Euclidean space on I.
Write e_j for the j-th coordinate vector and σ_j(x)=e_j−x_j x.
The vector x is arbitrary.
units.statement: For every ambient vector x and coordinate j, the radial inner product of the column σ_j(x) with x equals (1−‖x‖²)x_j.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Expand the inner product
substantive_formula_moves.text: Linearity separates the coordinate term x_j and the rank-one term x_j‖x‖².

units.scope_boundary: The factor 1−‖x‖² records the radial component at arbitrary ambient points.
units.proof_topology: expand radial inner product
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: No sphere assumption needed; ambient formula is correct.

assumption_inventory: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. The space is real Euclidean space on I.
Write e_j for the j-th coordinate vector and σ_j(x)=e_j−x_j x.
The vector x is arbitrary, and the sum runs over every coordinate.
units.statement: At every ambient vector x, the squared column norms of I−xxᵀ sum to d−2‖x‖²+‖x‖⁴, where d is the number of coordinates.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Compute one column norm
substantive_formula_moves.text: Expand the squared norm of e_j−x_j x using ‖e_j‖=1 and the coordinate inner product.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Sum the coordinate squares
substantive_formula_moves.text: Each constant one contributes to d, and the sum of the squared coordinates is ‖x‖².

units.scope_boundary: At a unit vector the squared column norm sum is d−1.
units.proof_topology: expand each squared norm; sum coordinate squares
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Correct for empty coordinate set as well. Boundary at a unit vector implies nonempty dimension.

assumption_inventory: The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality, $\|w\|=1$, and $\lambda\ge 0$.
The equality is valid for any ambient vector $u$. For tangent $u$, the first term is the directional derivative of the restricted test.
units.statement: Fix a unit vector $w\in\mathbb R^I$, an ambient real test $f$, a vector $u$, and a nonnegative temperature $\lambda$. Give the noise columns the amplitude $\sqrt{2\lambda}$ times the projected coordinate vectors. Give the drift the value $-u-\lambda(d-1)w$, where $d=|I|$. The ambient Itô generator equals the derivative in direction $-u$ plus $\lambda$ times the extrinsic sphere Laplacian.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Remove the noise amplitude from the trace
substantive_formula_moves.text: The Hessian is bilinear and the square root is taken of a nonnegative number. Squaring the amplitude and multiplying by one half gives the temperature.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Combine the radial drift and Hessian
substantive_formula_moves.text: The projected trace removes one radial Hessian entry. The radial drift gives the first-derivative term with factor $d-1$.

units.scope_boundary: The result identifies the ambient generator algebraically at a single unit state, including temperature zero.
units.proof_topology: extract squared noise amplitude; projected Hessian trace; combine radial drift
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Natural-math qualification: ordinary Df and D2f require derivatives to exist, while the source says any ambient test and gives no differentiability hypothesis. Either state twice Frechet differentiability at w or explicitly adopt a total-derivative convention for this algebraic lemma.

assumption_inventory: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
Each initial coordinate is strongly measurable at time zero. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive and has almost surely integrable time sections on the horizon.
The scalar test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K.
units.statement: For the actual Euclidean process built from initialized progressive time integrals and completed stochastic integrals, suppose its path lies in a compact K throughout the horizon almost surely. A scalar test twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K satisfies the terminal Itô identity almost surely, with the genuine completed derivative martingale starting at zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Use the three actual Taylor limits
substantive_formula_moves.text: The initialized drift supplies continuity, variation and measurability. Apply the first-order limit with its martingale, the half-Hessian limit and the Taylor residual limit. Choose one subsequence on which all three limits hold almost everywhere.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Telescope exactly at each dyadic level
substantive_formula_moves.text: On each cell, adding the linear term, half the Hessian term and the signed remainder gives the test increment exactly. These increments telescope between the first and last grid points.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Identify the almost-sure limit
substantive_formula_moves.text: The sum is the same for every grid level. On the event where the three terms converge, uniqueness of the limit gives the identity.

notation_inventory.text: The jth diffusion column has ith coordinate ηᵢⱼ.
The derivative integrands are specified by the theorem and are progressively square-integrable. The completed sum has M₀=0 for every sample.

units.scope_boundary: The identity holds at the specified positive terminal time. Compact containment holds for all times on one event of full measure.
units.proof_topology: obtain first-order, half-Hessian and residual limits; common almost-sure subsequence; exact Taylor telescoping; uniqueness
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: The derivative martingale must be the actual completed integrals with pointwise zero start and the all-s, a.e.-omega integrand identity. Compact fallback and time clipping are substantive bridges.

assumption_inventory: The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time. The sample measure is finite, and the coordinate set $I$ is finite with decidable equality.
The process $X$ takes values in the Euclidean unit sphere, is jointly measurable for the product of the time Borel and sample measurable structures, and is strongly progressive.

For the selected horizon $T\ge0$, the real deterministic temperature is Borel measurable on nonnegative time and bounded in absolute value pointwise on $[0,T]$. The square root is the total real square root.
The symbol $\ell_T$ denotes Lebesgue time restricted to $[0,T]$. The $L^2$ membership uses $\mu\otimes\ell_T$, in sample-first order.
units.statement: The definition constructs the strongly progressive product-space $L^2$ integrand for noise entry $(i,j)$ with the representative shown below.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Evaluate the projected column
substantive_formula_moves.text: The sphere projection has continuous coordinates, and the square root of the Borel temperature factor is Borel.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Package the horizon bound
substantive_formula_moves.text: Compactness bounds the projected coordinate on the sphere. The horizon bound on the temperature bounds its square-root factor, so the composed representative is strongly progressive with product-space $L^2$ membership.

units.scope_boundary: The representative is defined at all nonnegative times. The $L^2$ assertion uses the selected horizon.
units.proof_topology: Borel projected coefficient; compact-state bound; temperature bound; progressive composition and L2 packaging
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: No nonnegativity assumption needed for the total real sqrt constructor; defined on all times, L2 only on selected horizon.

assumption_inventory: The sample space carries a probability measure $P$, a filtration indexed by nonnegative real time satisfying the usual conditions, and a standard Euclidean Brownian motion relative to that filtration. The coordinate set $I$ is finite with decidable equality.
The process $X$ is jointly measurable and takes values in the Euclidean unit sphere $S$. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and ambient-vector-valued.
The deterministic temperature $\lambda$ is Borel measurable, nonnegative at each time, and bounded pointwise on each finite horizon. The ambient real test $f$ is $C^2$ at every point of $S$.

The process is strongly progressive. For each strictly positive horizon, its canonical integrated equation holds on one full-measure event simultaneously for every time up to that horizon and every coordinate.
The equation starts at $X_0$ and uses $b_i(t,w)=[-u(t,w)-\lambda(t)(|I|-1)w]_i$ and the completed stochastic integrals of $\sqrt{2\lambda(t)}[P_{X_t}e_j]_i$ against $B_j$, with $P_we_j=e_j-w_jw$.
The endpoints $a,b$ are arbitrary nonnegative times. The symbol $t^+$ denotes $\max(t,0)$.
The sphere generator is $\mathcal L_t f(w)=-Df(w)[u(t,w)]+\lambda(t)\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}}f(w)$, with $\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}}f(w)=\sum_j D^2f(w)[P_we_j,P_we_j]-(|I|-1)Df(w)[w]$.
units.statement: For the specified integrated sphere diffusion, set $\rho_t=(X_t)_\#P$, $F(t)=\int f(w)\,d\rho_{t^+}(w)$ and $B(t)=\int\mathcal L_{t^+}f(w)\,d\rho_{t^+}(w)$. The generator average $B$ is locally integrable on the real line. The expectation $F$ is absolutely continuous on every finite nonnegative interval and satisfies the signed balance and ordinary derivative below.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Supply integrable coefficient rows
substantive_formula_moves.text: Compactness and the horizon bound give bounded measurable drift and noise coordinates. Along the progressive process, each drift row is strongly progressive and time-integrable, while the noise construction provides product-space $L^2$ integrands.
substantive_formula_moves.detail: Use bounded_measurable_coefficient_along_progressive_process and the stored noise representative.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Apply the row formulation
substantive_formula_moves.text: Use the given canonical equation with these rows and initial coordinates. The row theorem yields the law balance with the explicit ambient generator.

units.scope_boundary: The SDE is an input. Its conclusion is a weak statement about time-dependent marginal expectations.
units.proof_topology: construct drift/noise rows; establish progressive integrability; apply law-balance row theorem
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: The canonical equation and strong progressiveness must supply time-zero measurability of X0 and all row hypotheses. No independent path continuity assumption is promised.

assumption_inventory: The sample space carries a probability measure. Time is nonnegative. The state space is compact and second countable, with its Borel measurable structure.
The process is jointly measurable and almost surely continuous in time. The test is continuous and the drift observable is jointly continuous.
For each nonnegative horizon there is a possibly horizon-dependent integrable real residual with mean zero. The pathwise balance with that residual holds almost surely.
units.statement: Let $X_t$ be a jointly measurable process taking values in a compact state space, with almost surely continuous paths. Let $g$ be a continuous real test and $A(t,x)$ a jointly continuous real drift observable. If at each horizon the increment of $g(X_t)$ equals the time integral of $A(s,X_s)$ plus an integrable centered residual almost surely, then the time derivative of the expectation is the expectation of $A(t,X_t)$. This is the ordinary derivative at positive times and the right derivative at time zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Take expectations in the horizon identity
substantive_formula_moves.text: Joint continuity bounds the drift observable on each compact time-by-state set. Fubini and the centered residual give the integral balance of expected values.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Differentiate the integral balance
substantive_formula_moves.text: Almost surely continuous paths give weakly continuous marginal laws. Joint continuity of the observable on compact sets gives a continuous expected drift. The fundamental theorem of calculus differentiates the balance.

units.scope_boundary: The residual is allowed to depend on the horizon. The claim concerns the fixed test expectation.
units.proof_topology: take expectations via Fubini and centered residual; show continuous expected drift; fundamental theorem
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Residuals may vary with horizon; no process-level martingale assumption should be introduced. At zero derivative must mean within nonnegative half-line.

assumption_inventory: The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is a probability measure. Standard vector Brownian motion is relative to the filtration, which satisfies the usual conditions.

The sphere-valued process is jointly measurable and its paths are almost surely continuous. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and takes ambient vector values. The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative.

At each positive horizon, the integrated rows use initial coordinates strongly measurable for the time-zero filtration σ-algebra, strongly progressive drift with almost surely integrable time sections, and progressive product-square-integrable Brownian integrands. The Euclidean representation agrees with the supplied sphere process at all times in that horizon almost surely.
Almost surely throughout each horizon, the drift is $-u(t,X_t)-\lambda_t(d-1)X_t$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_t}(e_j-(X_t)_jX_t)$. The test is $C^2$ at every sphere point.
units.statement: Let $X_t$ be a jointly measurable unit-sphere-valued process with almost surely continuous paths. Suppose its actual coordinates satisfy the specified integrated Brownian equation at every positive finite horizon with projected noise and its radial drift. For each twice continuously differentiable ambient test, the derivative of its expectation is the expected spherical generator. This is the ordinary derivative at positive times and the right derivative at time zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Obtain a centered increment on each horizon
substantive_formula_moves.text: On each positive horizon, the integrated Euclidean rows agree with the supplied sphere process throughout the horizon on a common full-measure event. Transfer the terminal Itô identity along this agreement. Its zero-start martingale has an integrable terminal value with mean zero. At horizon zero take the residual to be zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Put the balance on the real time axis
substantive_formula_moves.text: The horizon measure agrees with ordinary Lebesgue time after embedding the nonnegative interval into the reals. The sphere generator is jointly continuous because the test derivatives are continuous along the sphere and the projected trace is a finite sum.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Differentiate the expected observable
substantive_formula_moves.text: Apply the centered-residual derivative theorem to the same sphere process at all horizons.

units.scope_boundary: The input is a supplied integrated diffusion. The theorem gives the evolution of smooth test expectations for that process.
units.proof_topology: terminal sphere Ito identity; centered martingale residual; transport time measure; generator continuity; derivative theorem
dependency_edges: continuous derivative fields on compact sphere
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Continuity of the ambient derivative fields along sphere follows from C2-at-every-sphere-point. Horizon-dependent rows and exceptional events must remain horizon-dependent.

assumption_inventory: B is a real Brownian motion with the given filtration and measure; its law implies the measure is a probability measure. There are n≥0 cells with 0≤t₀≤⋯≤tₙ.
For every cell i, aᵢ is strongly measurable with respect to the filtration at tᵢ and belongs to L². Repeated times are allowed.
units.statement: Let aᵢ be square-integrable real weights measurable at the left endpoints of a nondecreasing finite deterministic time grid. For Brownian motion B relative to that filtration, the compensated weighted square-increment sum is square-integrable and satisfies the exact identity below.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Factor the diagonal second moments
substantive_formula_moves.text: The compensated square of one increment has mean zero and second moment 2(Δt)². It is independent of every left-endpoint measurable weight. This also proves L² integrability of each weighted term.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Eliminate the off-diagonal terms
substantive_formula_moves.text: For i<j, the earlier weighted increment and the j-th weight are measurable at tⱼ. The j-th centered increment is independent of their product and has mean zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Expand the square and retain only the diagonal
substantive_formula_moves.text: Each product is integrable by the L² bounds. Interchange finite sums and integrals, cancel the cross terms and substitute the diagonal moments.

units.scope_boundary: Weights need no almost-sure uniform bound. They may be dependent across cells; the required condition is left-endpoint measurability and a finite second moment.
units.proof_topology: diagonal centered Gaussian moment; past/future independence; off-diagonal cancellation; finite square expansion
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: Need explain integrability when multiplying earlier weighted increment and later L2 weight; Cauchy-Schwarz gives their L1 product. Source says products integrable via L2. No natural defect found.

assumption_inventory: E is a type, K⊆E, and k₀ is a specified member of K. The result does not assume compactness.
E has a measurable structure and K is a measurable set.
units.statement: If E is a measurable space and K is measurable, the map r:E→K is measurable for the induced subtype measurable structure.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Express the underlying map as a measurable piecewise map
substantive_formula_moves.text: The identity and the constant k₀ are measurable. Their piecewise combination on K is measurable, and the same map lifts to the subtype.

units.scope_boundary: No topology, compactness or continuity of r is asserted.
units.proof_topology: piecewise identity/constant map; subtype lift
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: No compactness/topology required. Selected fallback ensures nonempty K.

assumption_inventory: I is a finite coordinate set, E=ℝᴵ with its Euclidean norm, Ω carries a finite measure μ, and K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. The K-valued process X has measurable evaluations at every nonnegative time and almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T], where T>0.
For each j∈I the dyadic square-increment sum of coordinate j converges in measure to Qⱼ:Ω→ℝ.
units.statement: In a finite-dimensional Euclidean state space, it suffices that the square-increment sum of each coordinate converge in measure to its own real-valued Qⱼ. The vector Taylor residual sum then converges in measure to zero.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Sum the coordinate limits
substantive_formula_moves.text: Coordinate increments are measurable. A finite simultaneous subsequence argument allows their convergence-in-measure limits to be summed.

substantive_formula_moves.title: Recognize the Euclidean square norm
substantive_formula_moves.text: Interchange the two finite sums and use the Euclidean norm identity. This supplies the square-increment hypothesis of the dyadic residual theorem.

units.scope_boundary: The coordinate variation limits are inputs here. The result includes any finite coordinate set and claims convergence in measure, not pathwise convergence of the original sequence.
units.proof_topology: finite-sum coordinate in-measure limits; interchange finite sums; Euclidean norm identity; general residual theorem
units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_findings: No original-sequence almost-sure convergence should be claimed. No natural defect found.
